name: POTS: a delay whose repeats go down an old telephone line, for the delay slot
description: model27's own character delay (notes/69): every repeat passes a telephone line once more, so the echoes darken into a narrow, crackling band (350 Hz to 3 kHz, a little nasal at 1.5 kHz), move up 2 Hz a pass (a frequency shift, so the harmonics slowly part), fade in and out, now and then drop for a moment, and pick up a coarse codec grain, which leaves them as the tail dies away. Time and Fdbk keep their knobs and the stock delay's ranges; at the highest Fdbk the repeats sustain without running away (a leveler in the loop). Mono, the same repeat on both outputs; the loop at 24 kHz, the line the delay slot's (512 KiB, up to 5.46 s).

uses.name: POTS
uses.why: an effect of the delay slot: called as the stock delay 0x40057488 is, (out, in, P + 428), when the playing pattern chooses id 2; its line of 131 072 frames at 24 kHz is the slot's

emulation.pattern: notes/68 §17: instructions per block of the process called alone after its reset (the reset counted apart), on the OS 1.13 in tools/emu/test_fxslot.py section 6 (mcengine.py's counter): noise of +-2^28 into both channels, Time 0 and Fdbk 96 for the delay, Size 64 and Tone 96 for the reverb (x 256), the first block, then the mean and maximum over 21 blocks after 32 more

unchanged: the stock delay, whenever the playing pattern has not chosen POTS

emulation.tool: tools/emu/test_fxslot.py (Unicorn, the OS's own code, against the host build of tools/emu/pots_host.py, notes/69 §8, §14)
